steps.content: Deren seems surprised by your words. Then she chuckles, and narrows her eyes into slits, looking at you intensely.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Sounds like you know something that I don't.

options: Do you want me to tell you?

choices.text: Do you want me to tell you?

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: I'm intrigued, to be honest.
This factory has been around for a long time. Its name, Jaminet, is quite new though. It was adopted only three years ago.
Jaminet is also the surname of the man who manages the factory. But he is not the head of the factory, not in name at least; his sister is.
He was supposed to inherit this factory after his sister died. But he didn't want to; instead, he kept his title as vice president.

He hires special workers—a girl who ran away from home to escape being forced into marriage, a youngster who was forced to sell his organs to support his younger siblings, and many other members of the underprivileged who quarreled with fate.
Deren has an aha moment as the last of the workers walk out of the gate in twos and threes.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: This is?

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: The young woman in a suit at the end of the movie?
If her brother hadn't changed the name, I wouldn't have been able to find this place.
I talked to him a while back. He still remembered the day you met.
Deren looks at the nameplate, which looks much newer than the exterior of the factory. She nods, recalling.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: I remember too.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: His sister's journal was the inspiration for the movie.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: I found it in a junk shop.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Every item in a junk shop has a story. I really enjoy spending time there, looking for inspiration.
Deren takes you by the arm and leads you to the narrow flowerbed of roses under the nameplate. The two of you sit down on the edge, and she starts recounting the story about the journal.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: At first, I thought it belonged to a man, because it was full of notes on such subjects as finance, business, and politics. I only realized that it belonged to a woman when I came to the part where she complained about her mother, who had sent her to piano and violin lessons, instead of letting her stay in school with her younger brother.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: That's also when I realized that I was just as bigoted as her mother.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: The journal was a detailed account of her experiences and thoughts. I read through it in one night. In the pages, I saw a brave spirit who with every fiber of her being decried the injustices of her fate.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: She dreamed of starting a business, and her brother supported her. But her parents wouldn't allow it.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Her wings were clipped before she could learn to fly.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: She was forced into marriage with a family friend. As a married woman, she lived in a grandiose mansion, where she put her frustrations into words. In the end, she died in childbirth.
Your shackles start throbbing violently, a signal that Deren might be losing control. But you don't want to stop her from continuing.

The words in the journal have been etched on Deren's mind. That night, she read through the journal in the two hours between 5 p.m. to 7 p.m. And connected through the shackles, you can feel how the words are making Deren feel.
Now, the words have come alive, recreating the world of their writer before you and Deren again and again.
She was powerless but brave.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: When the final moment of her life came, she became a heroine to herself.
You reach out your hand, locking eyes with Deren. She gives a wan smile before putting her hand on yours.

The moment her hand touches yours, the shackles on your wrist come into contact with her hand. Presently, red thorns twist and turn, coming together to form an image of a young woman. Time freezes, as the image bursts into flames and burns to ashes.
The ashes fall, and time starts running again, as if nothing had happened.
The movie should've ended differently. The characters should've voiced their true thoughts at the end.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: I know. But there's nothing I could do about it. That's the ending the audience wanted to see.
The movie came up in my conversation with Mr. Jaminet.
Well, long story short, Mr. Jaminet changed the name of the factory because of the movie.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Really? But it's not unusual for a factory to be named after the person who runs it, right?
You point at a spot above her hat. She tips her head back and sees another word, surrounded by roses, before the word Jaminet on the nameplate: MISS.
Mr. Jaminet told me, although trapped in an unhappy marriage, his sister never gave up on her dream; she still wanted the world to hear her voice, and that's why she kept a journal.
After she passed away, the housekeeper sold the journal by accident, but as luck would have it, it ended up in your hands.
Mr. Jaminet saw his sister in the young woman in a suit who appears at the end of the movie... and countless other females just like her.
The ending was not exactly what he had expected, but he still thought it was a beautiful one. I understand why he felt that way. The young woman in the movie is not dead, after all.
Deren throws up her hands and sighs.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: I didn't give them enough credit. They must have gone to some trouble to salvage those shots from God knows where to make the final scene.
But this "beautiful" ending was what inspired him to revive his sister's dream, and let the world see his sister for who she was.
He changed the name of the factory and hired people like those in the movie, unfortunate but strong, while making his sister the permanent head of the factory.
You stand up and plant yourself before Deren.
Sorry, I shouldn't have brought you here. It was out of line, even if you did leave this notebook for me.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: No need to apologize. You can take me wherever you like, like when you took me to the MBCC.
Cough cough... that's not what I meant.
What I meant to say is... Don't let yourself be bound by what others think of you. Don't let yourself be defined by the label they gave you. Break free and be yourself.
Because you, Director Deren, are no ordinary person.
Deren rests her chin on her hand and looks up at you, a smile blossoming on her face.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: You're right. I'm a vicious person detained by the MBCC, an avoided-at-all-cost Sinner.
Well, Miss Sinner, would you like to peel off all the labels attached to you in front of everybody and let them see the movie that you've wanted them to see all along?
Deren is confused for a moment. She looks from you to the notebook in her hand and catches on to what you've just suggested.
She takes your extended hand and stands to her feet. She is wearing a mischievous grin on her face.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: I didn't expect you, Chief of the MBCC, to come up with such a crazy idea.
I hang around with lunatics like you, so...

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Thanks for the compliment. Lunatic... I quite like the moniker.
Gone are the last vestiges of daylight. In the dimness, you see the world reflected in Deren's eyes, bright like a star.
The days fly past. The long-awaited DisCars ceremony rolls around, and the whole Eastside comes alive.

In the days leading up to the ceremony, there has been much hype in Dillywood about Deren's new movie. It comes as no surprise that a large number of reporters have gathered outside the main venue for the ceremony.
But they are not in luck. They won't be able to see the director they are here for, since she is at the back entrance with you.
What is with you and back entrances?

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Well, it's quieter. I'm sure you don't want to get stuck in the crowd, surrounded by a bunch of blinking cameras, right?

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Relax. You're safe with me. I know my way around this place, though last time I was using this route to get out, not get in.
On the way here, you and Deren have avoided reporters that seem to have popped out of nowhere.
You and Deren walk into the hall and take your seats. The ceremony is heating up. But you soon realize that...

options: There's no escape from the inevitable...

choices.text: There's no escape from the inevitable...

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Have mercy on me, Chief. You're not gonna stand by and watch me suffer, are you?
Deren leans toward you ever so slightly and whispers in your ear, while maintaining her smile for the cameras.
The host seems hell-bent on taking advantage of the hype surrounding Deren, asking for her opinion before announcing the nominees for each award.

steps.speaker: Host
steps.content: Let's see... The next one is for Best Makeup.

steps.speaker: Host
steps.content: Any thoughts on this, Miss Deren?

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Makeup, or more broadly, the combination of makeup, costumes, and props, is indispensable to a great movie, though the Award for Best Makeup might not sound as important as the others.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Most often than not, how a character looks can mean the difference between alienating an audience and drawing them in, so...

steps.speaker: Host
steps.content: Well said, well said indeed. Now... without further ado, here are the nominees for achievement in makeup.
The protracted presentation of the awards ends, and the much-anticipated screening of upcoming movies begins.
The audience applauds and cheers, but not with excessive enthusiasm, at the end of each of the movies that come before Deren's.
The opinions given on the movies are contrived and stilted; they sound like work reports ghostwritten by some Eastside Sinners in a rush.
You understand why the audience is getting impatient. Deren's movie is the last to be shown.
We're next. Are you ready?

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: I can't wait.
A great cheer goes up from the crowd when the host announces that the next movie to be screened is Deren's.
You follow Deren onto the stage, asking the projectionist to sit offstage, and take over as a temporary projectionist.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Looks like everyone is looking forward to my new movie.

steps.speaker: Audience
steps.content: Absolutely!

steps.speaker: Audience
steps.content: That's why we are here!

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Thank you for your support. I'm honored.

steps.speaker: Audience
steps.content: We'll support you forever!

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Making movies isn't easy. The director's vision and skills are important, but a movie couldn't be made without input from the rest of the crew.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: They also have dreams, and they also turn their dreams into reality when a movie is made.

steps.speaker: Audience
steps.content: Bravo! Now show us the movie!

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: And film editing is not as easy as you might think.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Even when they have a clear idea about how a storyboard should look and what shots should be selected, film editors still have to cut footage and piece the strips of footage together.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: It can be the dullest job in the world if you don't have a passion for it.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: But film editing can also change how a movie turns out, and even decide the message it conveys.
The screen behind Deren remains black. The audience has lost their patience, urging her on with shouts.

steps.speaker: Audience
steps.content: What's with this long speech? Just show us the movie!

steps.speaker: Audience
steps.content: Yeah, show us the movie!

steps.speaker: Audience
steps.content: Miss Deren, show us how you've outdone yourself again!

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Do you really want to see it now?

steps.speaker: Audience
steps.content: Yes. Right Now!

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Are you sure?

steps.speaker: Audience
steps.content: Don't keep us in suspense!

steps.speaker: Audience
steps.content: Of course we are!

steps.speaker: Audience
steps.content: One hundred percent!
Deren turns off the microphone, walks to the center of the stage, and gives a smile, her eyes sweeping around the room.
Then she bows low to the audience.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: All right. Please enjoy...
You press the play button. The screen in the back flickers, and then an eerie red light spreads across it. Everyone is taken back to five years ago, to when the movie was first released.
There are murmurs in the crowd. "Isn't this supposed to be a new movie?" "Isn't this the movie from five years ago?"
Slowly but surely, everyone in the audience comes to realize that the movie they are watching couldn't be more different from the one from five years ago.
The shots are the same, but the way these shots have been edited and presented is different. Now they convey something entirely different.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: My best work. This is the movie that I wanted to show you five years ago.
As the movie plays on, the audience starts getting antsy.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Please stay where you are. The movie is not over yet. Okay?
Deren raises her hand and uses her power on the crowd. Their faces are frozen in different expressions.
You see the image in Deren's head: Rose petals falling from above and landing at the audience's feet.
More petals fall and gather around the many pairs of feet, keeping them from moving. The audience will not be released until the movie ends.

Chaos reigns. The audience watches, as the girl in white, tear-stained and helpless, screams at them, as the pale-face boy pulls out the vines that have sunk into his flesh, as the young woman in a suit burns down everything around her, sucks every bit of redness into her fountain pen, and uses it to write down her wildest dreams on a giant piece of paper.
Deren reaches out and takes your hand. She leads you up onto the stage. And the two of you bow to the crowd.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Thank you. Thanks to everyone who worked on this movie back in the day.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Thanks to everyone who helped me in making this movie possible.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Thanks to those who inspired me.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Thank you for making me become a "lunatic" again.
With that last sentence, Deren turns to you.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: I didn't walk the red carpet five years ago. Would you do me the honor of walking it with me?
Absolutely. After all, I did play a small part in reviving this great movie.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: You played much more than a small part.
Deren takes your hand. And with the big crowd watching, the two of you walk the red carpet and head toward the exit.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: You're the star of my eyes.
